thesis: Netflix has an operating-and-cash ownership case at an estimated 18.04x forward reference, with 13% revenue growth, 33.4% operating margin and $1.525bn Q2 FCF. The bull establishes that positive cash already follows $5.109bn content spending, preventing future commitments from being charged again to the current cash measure. Manageable stated net debt supports the case, while lower cash conversion and fee-enhanced headline valuation limit conviction.
strongest_counterexample: Q2 FCF fell from $2.267bn and margin from 34.1%; $25.107bn future content commitments and repurchases above quarterly FCF increase return sensitivity, while the $2.8bn fee prevents treating annual cash or trailing earnings as wholly recurring.
invalidation_conditions: Comparable Q2 FCF at or below zero after actual content spend and capex would invalidate demonstrated owner-cash generation.
Two consecutive quarters of year-on-year revenue decline with operating margin below 33.4% would falsify the profitable-growth thesis.
evidence_gaps: Exact cash-tax allocation associated with the termination fee is unavailable in the envelope, preventing an exact after-tax recurring H1 cash normalization.
decisive_factors: The termination fee is outside operating income and does not carry the recurring operating thesis.
Content costs already enter current cash; future commitments remain economically material without becoming all current debt.
